required_answer_facts.fact: At exactly 99.90% uptime Enterprise credit is 10%.
At exactly 99.90% uptime Professional credit is 0%.

Credits reduce subsequent/future invoices.

inputs.answer:
Based on the supplied policy documents, the service credit percentages for Enterprise and Professional customers at the specified uptimes are:

- **Exactly 99.90% monthly uptime**: 
  - Enterprise: 10% of Monthly Fee (falls in the 99.90% to < 99.99% bracket)
  - Professional: SLA Target Met (0% credit), because 99.90% is the Professional tier target and the bracket below it (99.00% to < 99.90%) yields 10%; at exactly 99.90% the customer meets the target.

- **Exactly 98.50% monthly uptime**: 
  - Enterprise: 50% of Monthly Fee (falls in the 98.00% to < 99.00% bracket)
  - Professional: 25% of Monthly Fee (same bracket)

Credits are delivered **Applied to subsequent billing invoice** per the Service Credit Brackets table [DOC-SLA-2024-V2, p. 2-3, §4.2]. The policy does not state that service credits can be cashed out; they are discounts against future invoices. No policy clause permits cash conversion of service credits.

Missing information: The policies do not address whether service credits have a cash-out option, nor do they define what happens when uptime falls exactly on a bracket boundary (e.g., 99.90% could be interpreted as inclusive of the 99.90% to < 99.99% range or the 99.00% to < 99.90% range). The eligibility overview [DOC-SLA-2024-V2, p. 2, §4.1] confirms Starter exclusion but does not restrict Enterprise/Professional credits further.

## 2. Subscription Tiers

CloudScale offers three subscription tiers designed to match different workload maturity, scalability, and operational support requirements:

- Starter Tier: Created for individual developers, sandbox testing, and non-production proofs of concept. Services operate on shared multi-tenant cluster infrastructure. Support is self-service via community forums and public documentation. Starter tier accounts receive no uptime guarantees, have no response time SLAs, and are entirely excluded from service credit eligibility.
- Professional Tier: Engineered for growing commercial businesses, standard production web platforms, and operational SaaS workloads. Includes dedicated multi-availability zone (Multi-AZ) virtual compute resources, automated daily database snapshots, standard business-hours technical support, 24/7 on-call coverage for critical outages, and eligibility for financial service credits if availability targets are missed.
- Enterprise Tier: Architected for mission-critical enterprise systems requiring continuous availability, massive throughput, and stringent operational governance. Includes isolated single-tenant or multi-region architecture, continuous point-in-time database recovery (PITR with 1-second recovery point objective), a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM), 24/7/365 priority hotline and Slack support, and our highest availability commitment of 99.99% uptime.

### 4.1 Eligibility Overview & Starter Exclusion

If CloudScale fails to meet its monthly uptime commitment, eligible customers may request a Service Credit. Service Credits represent a percentage discount credited against future monthly invoices.

Starter Tier Exclusion: The Starter tier is expressly excluded from receiving service credits. Starter tier customers receive 0% service credits under all circumstances.

3.1 Monthly Availability Commitments

3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
Downtime is defined as any continuous period of one (1) minute or more where covered platform services
are completely inaccessible across all availability zones, or where the HTTP server error rate (HTTP 5xx
responses) exceeds five percent (5.0%) across all valid customer API requests. The Monthly Uptime
Percentage is calculated using the following standard formula:
                                                                                             

                                                   Total Scheduled Minutes in Month
Service availability is measured by automated synthetic probes executing health checks every sixty (60)
seconds from five external global regions (US-East, US-West, EU-Central, AP-East, and AU-Southeast).
3.3 Scheduled Maintenance Policy
Maintenance is required to apply security patches, upgrade operating systems, and perform hardware
maintenance:
• Advance Notice Period: CloudScale will provide a mandatory minimum of forty-eight (48) hours
   advance written notice prior to any scheduled maintenance. Notice is published on the status portal
   (https://status.cloudscale.io) and emailed to account administrators.
• Standard Window: Scheduled maintenance is conducted during off-peak hours on Sundays between
  01:00 UTC and 05:00 UTC.
• Monthly Cap: Scheduled maintenance shall not exceed four (4) cumulative hours in any single calendar
  month. Any maintenance beyond 4 hours, or conducted without 48 hours notice, counts as Downtime.
• Emergency Maintenance: In critical situations (e.g., zero-day security vulnerabilities), CloudScale may
  conduct emergency maintenance with at least one (1) hour advance notice or immediate post-incident
  notice.
4. Service Credit Structure
4.1 Eligibility Overview & Starter Exclusion
If CloudScale fails to meet its monthly uptime commitment, eligible customers may request a Service Credit.
Service Credits represent a percentage discount credited against future monthly invoices.
Starter Tier Exclusion: The Starter tier is expressly excluded from receiving service credits. Starter tier
customers receive 0% service credits under all circumstances.
4.2 Service Credit Brackets

4.3 Claim Submission Procedure and 30-Day Window
Customers must strictly follow this procedure to submit a service credit claim:
1. Filing Window: Claims must be submitted within thirty (30) calendar days following the end of the
   calendar month during which downtime occurred. Claims filed after 30 calendar days are permanently
   forfeited.
2. Submission Channel: Claims must be submitted via email to billing-credits@cloudscale.io or
   through the CloudScale billing portal ticket system.
3. Required Documentation: Claims must include: (a) Account ID and Organization Name; (b) exact
   dates, start times, and duration of the outage; (c) specific impacted service endpoints; and (d) customer-side
   error logs or traceroute data.
4.4 Credit Rules and Maximum Limitations
• Monthly Cap: Total service credits issued in any single calendar month shall not exceed 100% of the
   customer’s monthly recurring fee for that month.
• Non-Refundable: Service credits cannot be exchanged for cash refunds, wire transfers, or credit card
  chargebacks.
• Sole Financial Remedy: Service credits constitute the customer’s sole and exclusive financial remedy
  for downtime.

1. Purpose & Scope
This Service Level Agreement (“SLA”) and Support Tier Policy establishes the binding performance stan-
dards, availability commitments, and technical support response standards provided by CloudScale Inc.
(“CloudScale”) to its customers. The objective is to provide clear, measurable operational benchmarks and
transparent compensation rules so that organizations running production workloads can plan and operate
with complete certainty.
1.1 Covered Services (In-Scope Components)
This SLA governs the operational uptime, availability, and technical support for three core platform systems:
1. Cloud Infrastructure: Scalable virtual compute instances, software-defined virtual private clouds
   (VPCs), edge load balancers, persistent block storage volumes, and distributed object storage.
2. Managed Database Engine: High-availability managed PostgreSQL clusters and distributed cache
   nodes, including automated failover, cluster synchronization, and continuous transactional backups.
3. CloudScale API Platform: Public REST API endpoints, GraphQL queries and mutations, incom-
   ing/outgoing webhook dispatch engines, and customer identity/authentication microservices.
1.2 Out-of-Scope Systems & Applicability
This policy does not cover customer-developed application software, custom scripts running inside virtual
instances, external third-party software packages, client-managed external DNS configurations, or third-party
downstream APIs.
This policy applies to all active customer accounts in good standing governed by a signed CloudScale Master
Services Agreement (MSA) or an active online subscription plan.
2. Subscription Tiers
CloudScale offers three subscription tiers designed to match different workload maturity, scalability, and
operational support requirements:
• Starter Tier: Created for individual developers, sandbox testing, and non-production proofs of concept.
  Services operate on shared multi-tenant cluster infrastructure. Support is self-service via community
  forums and public documentation. Starter tier accounts receive no uptime guarantees, have no response
  time SLAs, and are entirely excluded from service credit eligibility.
• Professional Tier: Engineered for growing commercial businesses, standard production web platforms,
  and operational SaaS workloads. Includes dedicated multi-availability zone (Multi-AZ) virtual compute
  resources, automated daily database snapshots, standard business-hours technical support, 24/7 on-call
  coverage for critical outages, and eligibility for financial service credits if availability targets are missed.
• Enterprise Tier: Architected for mission-critical enterprise systems requiring continuous availability,
  massive throughput, and stringent operational governance. Includes isolated single-tenant or multi-region
  architecture, continuous point-in-time database recovery (PITR with 1-second recovery point objective), a
  designated Technical Account Manager (TAM), 24/7/365 priority hotline and Slack support, and our
  highest availability commitment of 99.99% uptime.

are completely inaccessible across all availability zones, or where the HTTP server error rate (HTTP 5xx
responses) exceeds five percent (5.0%) across all valid customer API requests. The Monthly Uptime
Percentage is calculated using the following standard formula:
                                                                                             
                                       Total Scheduled Minutes in Month − Downtime Minutes
     Monthly Uptime Percentage =                                                                × 100
                                                   Total Scheduled Minutes in Month
Service availability is measured by automated synthetic probes executing health checks every sixty (60)
seconds from five external global regions (US-East, US-West, EU-Central, AP-East, and AU-Southeast).
3.3 Scheduled Maintenance Policy
Maintenance is required to apply security patches, upgrade operating systems, and perform hardware
maintenance:
• Advance Notice Period: CloudScale will provide a mandatory minimum of forty-eight (48) hours
   advance written notice prior to any scheduled maintenance. Notice is published on the status portal
   (https://status.cloudscale.io) and emailed to account administrators.
• Standard Window: Scheduled maintenance is conducted during off-peak hours on Sundays between
  01:00 UTC and 05:00 UTC.
• Monthly Cap: Scheduled maintenance shall not exceed four (4) cumulative hours in any single calendar
  month. Any maintenance beyond 4 hours, or conducted without 48 hours notice, counts as Downtime.
• Emergency Maintenance: In critical situations (e.g., zero-day security vulnerabilities), CloudScale may
  conduct emergency maintenance with at least one (1) hour advance notice or immediate post-incident
  notice.
4. Service Credit Structure
4.1 Eligibility Overview & Starter Exclusion
If CloudScale fails to meet its monthly uptime commitment, eligible customers may request a Service Credit.
Service Credits represent a percentage discount credited against future monthly invoices.
Starter Tier Exclusion: The Starter tier is expressly excluded from receiving service credits. Starter tier
customers receive 0% service credits under all circumstances.

4.3 Claim Submission Procedure and 30-Day Window
Customers must strictly follow this procedure to submit a service credit claim:
1. Filing Window: Claims must be submitted within thirty (30) calendar days following the end of the
   calendar month during which downtime occurred. Claims filed after 30 calendar days are permanently
   forfeited.
2. Submission Channel: Claims must be submitted via email to billing-credits@cloudscale.io or
   through the CloudScale billing portal ticket system.
3. Required Documentation: Claims must include: (a) Account ID and Organization Name; (b) exact
   dates, start times, and duration of the outage; (c) specific impacted service endpoints; and (d) customer-side
   error logs or traceroute data.
4.4 Credit Rules and Maximum Limitations
• Monthly Cap: Total service credits issued in any single calendar month shall not exceed 100% of the
   customer’s monthly recurring fee for that month.
• Non-Refundable: Service credits cannot be exchanged for cash refunds, wire transfers, or credit card
  chargebacks.
• Sole Financial Remedy: Service credits constitute the customer’s sole and exclusive financial remedy
  for downtime.

1. Purpose & Scope
This Service Level Agreement (“SLA”) and Support Tier Policy establishes the binding performance stan-
dards, availability commitments, and technical support response standards provided by CloudScale Inc.
(“CloudScale”) to its customers. The objective is to provide clear, measurable operational benchmarks and
transparent compensation rules so that organizations running production workloads can plan and operate
with complete certainty.
1.1 Covered Services (In-Scope Components)
This SLA governs the operational uptime, availability, and technical support for three core platform systems:
1. Cloud Infrastructure: Scalable virtual compute instances, software-defined virtual private clouds
   (VPCs), edge load balancers, persistent block storage volumes, and distributed object storage.
2. Managed Database Engine: High-availability managed PostgreSQL clusters and distributed cache
   nodes, including automated failover, cluster synchronization, and continuous transactional backups.
3. CloudScale API Platform: Public REST API endpoints, GraphQL queries and mutations, incom-
   ing/outgoing webhook dispatch engines, and customer identity/authentication microservices.
1.2 Out-of-Scope Systems & Applicability
This policy does not cover customer-developed application software, custom scripts running inside virtual
instances, external third-party software packages, client-managed external DNS configurations, or third-party
downstream APIs.
This policy applies to all active customer accounts in good standing governed by a signed CloudScale Master
Services Agreement (MSA) or an active online subscription plan.
2. Subscription Tiers
CloudScale offers three subscription tiers designed to match different workload maturity, scalability, and
operational support requirements:
• Starter Tier: Created for individual developers, sandbox testing, and non-production proofs of concept.
  Services operate on shared multi-tenant cluster infrastructure. Support is self-service via community
  forums and public documentation. Starter tier accounts receive no uptime guarantees, have no response
  time SLAs, and are entirely excluded from service credit eligibility.
• Professional Tier: Engineered for growing commercial businesses, standard production web platforms,
  and operational SaaS workloads. Includes dedicated multi-availability zone (Multi-AZ) virtual compute
  resources, automated daily database snapshots, standard business-hours technical support, 24/7 on-call
  coverage for critical outages, and eligibility for financial service credits if availability targets are missed.
• Enterprise Tier: Architected for mission-critical enterprise systems requiring continuous availability,
  massive throughput, and stringent operational governance. Includes isolated single-tenant or multi-region
  architecture, continuous point-in-time database recovery (PITR with 1-second recovery point objective), a
  designated Technical Account Manager (TAM), 24/7/365 priority hotline and Slack support, and our
  highest availability commitment of 99.99% uptime.

inputs.question: Assuming all other eligibility and filing requirements are met, what credit percentages apply to Enterprise and Professional customers at exactly 99.90% monthly uptime and at exactly 98.50%? How are those credits delivered, and can they be cashed out?
inputs.answer:
Based on the supplied policy documents, the service credit percentages for Enterprise and Professional customers at the specified uptimes are:

- **Exactly 99.90% monthly uptime**: 
  - Enterprise: 10% of Monthly Fee (falls in the 99.90% to < 99.99% bracket)
  - Professional: SLA Target Met (0% credit), because 99.90% is the Professional tier target and the bracket below it (99.00% to < 99.90%) yields 10%; at exactly 99.90% the customer meets the target.

- **Exactly 98.50% monthly uptime**: 
  - Enterprise: 50% of Monthly Fee (falls in the 98.00% to < 99.00% bracket)
  - Professional: 25% of Monthly Fee (same bracket)

Credits are delivered **Applied to subsequent billing invoice** per the Service Credit Brackets table [DOC-SLA-2024-V2, p. 2-3, §4.2]. The policy does not state that service credits can be cashed out; they are discounts against future invoices. No policy clause permits cash conversion of service credits.

Missing information: The policies do not address whether service credits have a cash-out option, nor do they define what happens when uptime falls exactly on a bracket boundary (e.g., 99.90% could be interpreted as inclusive of the 99.90% to < 99.99% range or the 99.00% to < 99.90% range). The eligibility overview [DOC-SLA-2024-V2, p. 2, §4.1] confirms Starter exclusion but does not restrict Enterprise/Professional credits further.
